chunks: Our Lord, and give us what You promised us through Your prophets; and do not put us to shame on the Day of Resurrection. Indeed, You do not fail in Your promise.

key_terms.إِنَّكَ لَا تُخْلِفُ الْمِيعَادَ: Indeed, You do not fail in Your promise

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of the prophets' supplication in Surah Al-Imran verse 194?
ai.summary: Known as Du'a al-Anbiya, this verse is recited by the Imams as a model for communal supplication, emphasizing the continuity of divine promise from the Prophets to the Ahl al-Bayt. It highlights the theological concept of 'wa'd' (promise) and serves as a reminder of God's fidelity to His covenant, particularly in the context of the ultimate success of the righteous against their adversaries.
